detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Interface engine.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype="hl7:v2"`, `msg_type="ADT"`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Reconciliation job for ADT A03 without matching A01; monitor duplicate PV1 segments.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=interfaces sourcetype="hl7:v2" msg_type="ADT*"
| search routing_status="FAIL" OR ErrorCode!="0"
| stats count, values(pid) as patients by sending_facility, receiving_system
| sort -count
```

Understanding this SPL

**ADT Message Routing Failures** — ADT misroutes leave wrong census in downstream systems (lab, HIE), affecting care and billing.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype="hl7:v2"`, `msg_type="ADT"`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Interface engine. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: interfaces; **sourcetype**: hl7:v2. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=interfaces, sourcetype="hl7:v2". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• Applies an explicit `search` filter to narrow the current result set.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by sending_facility, receiving_system** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.


Step 3 — Validate
Run the search on recent production data, spot-check a handful of results against the source system or operational runbooks (cash operations, EHR, payment gateway, etc.), and adjust thresholds to match your seasonal patterns and test windows so teams are not flooded with noise.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Table (failed routes), Sankey (facility → system), Line chart (failure trend).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Interface engine — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=hl7:v2 into interfaces. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`receiving_system, sending_facility`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
